page.layout: One column of running text, set in roman and italic, with a narrow strip of marginal notes cropped at the right edge of the scan. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword. Printed page number and running head at the top of the page.

main_text.p: suæ principiis, aut ex factis factorum que ratione, prout à suarum partium nec suspectæ fidei historicis narrantur judicare licet non esse cur sibi calumnian à nostris fieri tàm fidenter clamitent. Interim sententiam illam dum nolunt videri suam, aut falsam aut impiam tacitò agnoscunt. Increpant aliquoties Prophetæ Reges Judæ, & præ cæteris Ezechiel toto fere capite decimo septimo quòd fidem Babyloniæ regibus juratam non servassent. Locus est insignis, & quem memini alicubi Chrysostomum & fusè pulchre admodum explicare. Quin Gentilium historiis nobilitata est Regili, aliorúmque hac in parte fides : qui & hostibus & Pœnis (perfidissimæ gentis) quod jurejurando intercedente promferant, vel cum certo capitis periculo censuerunt oportere præstari. Regulum hoc elogio ornat Silius, compellans um quasi per apostrophen

p.i: Qui longum semper fama gliscente pi[?] ævum, Infidis servasse fidem memorabere Ponis.

main_text.p: Objicies fortasse vulgaria illa, Fallere fallentem pro fraude non habendum,

page.notes: Right-hand margin: only the first letters of notes are visible, cut off by the edge of the scan. These are illegible and are not transcribed. Line ends at the right edge are cropped, so some words are incomplete (for example "calumnian", "juratam", "compellans", "promferant"). They are copied as far as they show; the rest is not reconstructed. "pi[?]" at the end of the first verse line: the word is cut off by the scan edge. Probably "per", but not legible. "Regili": the word breaks across lines ("Regi" / "li"), and no hyphen is visible; written whole. Long s has been rendered as s throughout (for example "suæ", "sibi", "esse", "insignis"), following the rule. Running head: the printed "Juramenti" is written as "Iuramenti", following the rule on i/j.
